title: Beef Stew
description: Tender chunks of beef slowly braised with red wine, carrots, potatoes and thyme in a rich, thick gravy. Worth every minute.
equipment: Large Dutch oven with a lid

image.alt: A bowl of beef stew with carrots and potatoes

steps.text: Heat the oven to {temp 325F oven}. Pat the beef dry, season with 1 tsp of the salt and the pepper, and toss with the flour.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in the pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in batches, without crowding, until well browned on several sides, {time 5-6 min} per batch. Move to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil and the onion and cook until soft, {time 5 min}, scraping up the browned bits. Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir for {time 1 min}.

Pour in the wine and simmer for {time 2 min}. Add the broth, Worcestershire, thyme, bay leaves, the remaining salt and the beef with its juices. Bring to a simmer, cover and move to the oven for {time 1 hr 30 min}.
Stir in the carrots and potatoes, cover and return to the oven until the beef and vegetables are fork-tender, {time 45-60 min}.
Remove the bay leaves, stir in the peas and let them warm through for {time 5 min}. Taste for salt and serve.

notes: Chuck is the right cut: its connective tissue melts into tender, juicy meat. Lean cuts turn dry.
Like most stews, it’s better the next day. Keeps 4 days, or freeze (without potatoes, which go grainy) for 3 months.
